run.Original_Project_description: The Oxford Vaccine Group is currently undertaking a human infection model investigating the clinical and immunological effects of repeated exposure to enteric fever. Multiple samples are collected over a 1-year period following challenge with either Salmonella Typhi or Salmonella Paratyphi A, in naive or previously exposed individuals. Gut flora have been shown to influence the permeability of the epithelial layer to gastrointestinal bacteria and the local immune response to infection in rodent models. To provide a detailed picture of changes to microbiome content, amplification of the bacterial 16S rRNA genes and WGS is being performed from stool samples. This project will use WGS and 16s RNA sequencing to look at the Microbiota This data is part of a pre-publication release. For information on the proper use of pre-publication data shared by the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute (including details of any publication moratoria), please see http://www.sanger.ac.uk/datasharing/
